It all started with a small spar.

Mydei met Phainon on a morning, completely normal, he asked for a sparring session. And of course, Phainon obliged, excited as they both headed toward the training area.

Eventually, they emptied the place; it was just the two of them. People found it too intimidating once the two strong Alphas started throwing punches at each other. The air around them was thick —others couldn’t breathe in it. So, they were left alone.

When it all started, Mydei had been winning. He had the upper hand. Phainon was using a wooden sword like a fool, shoving that thing toward Mydei. And, as you’d guess, the Strife’s demigod didn’t need much effort—the wooden sword broke into shreds with one punch as Phainon tried to dodge.

Mydei huffed, more confident now, at the other’s stupid face, he was looking at the broken sword like it had personally offended him.

“Come on now,” Mydei started, “Draw Dawnmaker, Deliverer.” He said it in a tone almost sly. “Fighting a demigod with a wooden sword? How foolish,” he laughed, lunging at the other, throwing in another attack, forcing Phainon to draw the real blade.

To his satisfaction, the other Alpha did. Dawnmaker was summoned instantly to block Mydei’s attack, just as it was about to graze his cheek. Both of them were pushed back.

“Just like that,” Mydei said, satisfied.

Phainon shook his head. “You know, it’s only fair if I didn’t use my sword either,” he said, though he knew Mydei’s strength, and that without his sword, he was at a disadvantage. Not that he’d admit it out loud.

“Come on now, you’re supposed to defeat me one day, remember?” Mydei said, so nonchalant. “And how will you face me as I am—Strife itself?”

He charged in again, continuing his attacks, giving Phainon no time to even think of dodging. And so, things escalated from there.

They were fighting, with Mydei holding the upper hand.

…Well, in the beginning.

There might’ve been a minor miscalculation. On Mydei’s end, today. He got a tiny bit clumsy.

Like—

It was all going fine. He’d dodged a swing, landed a solid kick, even caught Phainon off-balance once and swept the bastard’s legs. Phainon had hit the dirt laughing, Dawnmaker barely missing his own foot.

“You’re in high spirits today, Mydeimos,” Phainon had teased, brushing mud off his cheek.

“Shut up and fight,” Mydei muttered, already charging again.

Now?

Now he was pinned to the ground. Chest heaving. Sweat dripping into his eye. Dawnmaker’s hilt dug into his left wrist like a warning, while Phainon’s wrist pressed against his throat, firm and steady. The other’s full weight was on Mydei’s hips, pinning him down.

Their faces were so close, too close just inches apart, that Mydei could feel the other’s breath against his face.

Phainon grinned, loose and cocky, white hair falling in his face. “Do you yield?”

Mydei bared his teeth.

“Never.”

It wasn’t just pride. It was the way Phainon was looking at him. Smug, flushed, glowing under the training ground sky like he knew he had him. Like he’d win.

And no. That wouldn’t do.

Mydei’s gaze flicked to the black leather choker hanging half-torn from Phainon’s neck.

He’d caught it mid-tumble earlier. Didn’t mean to. Mostly. But he hadn’t exactly let it go, either. It dangled loose now, showing the edge, and most of the golden sun tattoo underneath.

Mydei smirked, lips twitching.

There.

His way out.

Both of them never shied away from cheating. And what he was planning wasn’t cheating, per se— just a dirty trick. And this would be no different. Both of them had their own wits and tricks when it came to their little challenges. Plus kremnoan worriers are known to be savages during battles, so this will be not that far off for him.

And so he tried to feel his hands.

His left arm? It was still stuck.

But his right arm? Nearly free. He flexed his fingers, shifting it slightly, and, his wrist slipped from Phainon’s grip.

Before Phainon could react, Mydei reached up—and yanked the rest of the choker clean off.

Phainon flinched.

That was the crack he needed.

Mydei lunged forward and bit him—right over the sun tattoo.

It was sharp and deep. Not enough to hurt badly, but enough to draw blood.

Phainon’s body arched in surprise, a startled, raw sound ripping from his throat. The pressure on Mydei’s wrists loosened.

Mydei shoved him off hard, rolling up into a seated position, spitting the taste of blood from his mouth.

He braced for a hit or comeback. Something stupid like, ‘Really? Teeth?’ Or a smug, ’Finally using your mouth for something useful?’.

But unlike he expected non came, only silence.

And for too long, There were no insults. No flinging Dawnmaker at his face. Not even giggling.

“…Was the Great Deliverer silenced by a mere bite?” he laughed, finally turning to face the man.

But when his eyes caught the other, Phainon was still lying on his side, haven’t recovered from the push, eyes wide, with fingers hovering over the bite mark. Breathing shallow. Mouth shut. Not making any effort to stand or even move.

The weird part wasn’t that he was still and quiet.

It was his eyes.

They weren’t blue.

They were gold. Bright, glazed over, and staring past Mydei, like he wasn’t even there.

Mydei squinted. “HKS?”

That usually worked. It usually snapped him out of his head, angered him, provoked a reaction. But instead of replying, Phainon’s dazed eyes focused on him.

And something in Mydei’s gut turned at the way the other was looking at him.

Before he could even process it, or prepare another comeback.

Phainon crawled.

Hah… did he really hit his head that hard when Phainon pinned him before? had his healing dulled that much? Because why was the destined deliverer of Okhema crawling toward him.

On his hands and knees.

Crawling.

Across the dirt.

Right toward him.

Mydei blinked once.

Then again.

Mydei found himself inching back, instinctively trying to put distance between them, between whatever it was Phainon was trying to do. Fear? No. There was no word for fear in the kremnoen language. It was something else entirely. The sheer aftershock of processing the sight of the other approaching him like that.

To his luck and horrible horrible fate, his back hit the weapon rack behind him, halting him cold.

“Hey—”

Phainon paid him no mind. He just kept moving. Climbing onto him, settling into his lap without a word. Just… settled there. Legs folded to the side, arms looping loosely around his waist. He pressed his cheek against Mydei’s bare chest, still breathing heavy but… calm.

“Deliverer.”

He felt the others weight, heat, breathe just everything.

“Phainon”

Nothing.

“…Pull yourself together,” Mydei said, hands on his shoulders, trying—gently, forcefully—to pry him off.

Phainon whined.

It was a soft, pathetic noise that made something in Mydei’s spine curl.

Phainon’s grip tightened as he nuzzled further in, letting out another whine like this was exactly where he wanted to be.

And Mydei?

Mydei panicked.

Red crystals were growing around the arena, and around them. He should probably get them under control, but—

By Nikador’s name—

What the fuck.

Why was his equal, his rival, and the very person he’d told his sole weakness to, rubbing his cheek into his chest?

Mydei found one of his hands reaching toward Phainon, fingers threading through white hair before gripping it, pulling gently, making the other tilt his head up from where it had been tucked against his chest.

He meant to say something.

But the words caught in his throat.

Phainon’s cheek still rested against his chest, stubbornly unmoved, yet his eyes—gold, with barely a flicker of blue left—were looking up at him. Confused, flushed but content. Adoration shimmered through the haze, soft and disarming, despite the unkind grip Mydei still had on his hair.

Mydei’s face burned. His hand let go, gaze breaking away. His heartbeat was… not normal.

And Phainon—delirious, oblivious—just sighed softly… and melted further into his chest, as if the world outside didn’t exist.

Calming himself, Mydei dared a glance down at the white-haired Alpha curled against him. Clinging like they hadn’t been sparring minutes ago. Like they hadn’t just been at each other’s throats minutes ago.

“…What did I do?” he muttered to himself, horrified.

And Titans, he hears purring.

Hyacine had just finished wrapping a patient’s shoulder when her teleslate buzzed.

The senders name blinked at the front.

It read Mydeimos.

She blinked. Mydei never messaged her first.

Unless.

She saw typing then a pause.

To typing again.

Her eyes narrowed into a frown.

There was another pause a bit longer this time.

Then ...

And that’s how they ended up here, In Twilight Courtyard. On a bed. With a Phainon who’s refusing to let go.

It had been mortifying carrying the alpha across the city like a toddler. Mydei had to assure the worried citizens that their ‘Beloved Deliverer’ was just injured and not... well. Whatever else they might’ve assumed.

He sighs now, arms full of a clingy, oversized alpha.

After explaining everything, Aglaea, who likely saw or heard everything through her threads, had seated herself in the infirmary with her chin perched in her hands, visibly thinking. Thoughtful. Knowing.

Hyacine, on the other hand, was struggling to examine the bite mark. Phainon kept trying to hide his neck, nuzzling stubbornly into Mydei’s shoulder, refusing to be touched.

The moment her fingers accidentally brushed his hand, Phainon growled low. Then whimpered out an apologetic whine.

Hyacine groaned under her breath, frustrated.

“So… anything?” Mydei asked, adjusting his grip on the massive alpha purring in his lap him.

“Well,” Hyacine said, a bit flushed, “Um-“ she looked around trying to word it out and said.

“…it looks like you claimed him.”

A chunk red crystals bursted through the ceiling as his soul evacuates his body for a second.

No one commented about the crystal.

Hyacine sits beside the bed and folds her arms with the calm of a person who has absolutely no idea what to say that’ll make the situation better “Good news or bad news?”

“Good first,” he says grimly.

“The mark is temporary. It’ll fade in a day or two, and shouldn’t have lasting effects.”

He exhales.

“…And the bad?”

“You accidentally dragged him into alpha subspace… and,” omega healer says hesitating, clearly weighing the words.

Mydei’s patience snapped. “And what.”

Aglaea, who’d been quiet until now finally spoke. She always sounded sensitive when it came to the topic of anything regarding the Deliverer, but Mydei didn’t have the bandwidth to unpack that particular favoritism right now.

“It’s a wonder why his alpha is clingy toward you,” she said flatly. “If it were any other alpha, it might’ve ended in bloodshed.”

Mydei blinked. He wasn’t particularly educated on secondary gender dynamics, never had the time or need to be. He was a warrior. And a prince. He didn’t get to empathize with things like this.

“But… he’s an alpha,” he said, stupidly. Because that was obvious.

“That he is,” Aglaea replied, unbothered. “Which is why it’s shocking.”

“What do you mean?”

“His alpha should be biting your head off for claiming him. Instead…” She gestured to Phainon on his lap, still purring like a satisfied cat. “He’s submitting to you.”

Oh

Submit

wait

Submit?

The word hit Mydei like a charging Doromas as another crystal popped behind the bed. This time it made Hyacine flinch a bit.

He opened his mouth. And closed. Opened again. And closed. His scent soured slightly with confusion.

To that Phainon reacted immediately. His distress bloomed in tandem, nosing at Mydei’s neck, hands making their way to grip on to Mydei’s shouldes so he can move more freely, all while trying to scent him back to calm.

It worked. Which was… more concerning.

The other two awkwardly cleared their throats.

“Ahem. Anyway. What’s done is done,” Aglaea declared, brushing nonexistent dust from her dress standing up. “I have important matters to attend to, and I suppose the punishment for both of you for your recklessness is being served as we speak. I won’t tack on more.” Her eyes narrowed. “Take care of him.”

And so she left without another word.

Mydei let out the breath he’d been holding.

Phainon’s scent curled around him. Warm, calm, grounding. But even that couldn’t quiet the internal screaming.

“I’ll pay for the ceiling” he finally said, “and the wall”

Hyacine gave him a sympathetic look. That said ‘it was fine’ before comforting him. “I’m sure you were unaware, Lord Mydei,” she said gently. Not about the wall or the ceiling just the situation “I can sedate him until he’s normal, if you’re uncomfortable.”

“No,” Mydei said, too quickly.

Hyacine smiled faintly, then outlined what little was known. Submissive alphas were rare. There wasn’t much research on how to care for one, especially not one stuck in subspace. Her only recommendation: take him home and let him rest. She healed what wounds she could, despite Phainon reflexively trying to nip at her fingers for touching him. He looked deeply confused by his own behavior—and guilty, every time he lashed out.

Mydei sighed. Of course the other alpha was new to this too.

They left the infirmary shortly after.

“Walk, Deliverer,” Mydei said, flatly. No way was he explaining this mess to passersby. No way was he carrying him again, not with rumors already no doubt bubbling.

Phainon blinked up at him like a kicked puppy and stood obediently.

Mydei groaned. “Don’t do that.”

Phainon tilted his head.

“Don’t listen to what I say so easily, you idiot,” he muttered, trying to preserve the last shreds of the other alpha’s dignity. Because surely…surely—Phainon would be mortified once this haze wore off.

They were almost to the outside the courtyard when Phainon reached out, grabbing Mydei’s arm.

And Mydei turned.

Phainon looked at him like he wanted to hold hands. His eyes were wide-eyed and hopeful, staring at his arm then to his face.

Mydei instinctively flinched, and Phainon immediately withdrew his hands and looked down, fidgeting with his fingers. Ashamed.

Really?

He was trying to save the other’s pride here, and this is what he get?

Mydei dragged a frustrated hand over his face before sighing and stabbing his own hand forward. He grasped Phainon’s and dragged him along without looking back. If he looked, he’d see those impossibly big bright gold-and-blue eyes again.

They reached Mydei’s quarters in silence ignoring all the curious glances and whispers. He then opened the door, and stormed inside.

Still holding Phainon’s hand.

Mydei lets out a tired sigh as he drags both of them into his kitchen.

Even though he's bone-deep exhausted from everything that happened today, they still needed to eat. Even if he didn’t, Phainon would surely appreciate food.

He makes Phainon sit on the chair near the counter while the other Alpha dumbly stares at the action, like a lost puppy. And just as he’s about to let go, Phainon makes a noise. Because of course he does.

They haven’t detached from each other since the fateful bite incident. So yeah, this will be hard. Even though Mydei’s patience is wearing thin—mostly because of the shock he went through in the past few quints, he just has to roll with it. Because, yes, it was kind of his fault.

So Mydei ever-so-kindly snaps his hand free, ignoring the other’s whines. Because by Strife’s name, the whining. That is the last sound he ever imagined hearing from the other’s mouth. He hadn’t uttered a single word, it was all just noises. Again it was the last thing Mydei imagined when he asked for a sparring session this morning. Not that he absolutely hated it(his own alpha was annoyingly loving whatever was going on here which made Mydei somewhat embarrassed) and He does enjoy the other’s attention. It’s that everything about this catches him off guard, and he does not like that.

He hurries to make them something. He had some leftover bater from today’s breakfast—golden honey cakes.

“Pancakes for dinner,” he mutters, disappointed. But his brain can’t muster the energy to make anything else right now. So he makes a few. He can feel eyes drilling into his back, examining every movement, but he ignores it and proceeds to plate them both.

He sits across from Phainon, much to the clingy Alpha’s disappointment.

He’ll live, Mydei thinks.

And starts eating. He’s halfway through his plate when he notices the other hasn’t touched his. He’s just staring.

Titans, you can see other’s imaginary dog ears droop.

And Mydei curses. He finishes his plate quickly before moving to sit beside Phainon, picking up a fork and feeding him.

This is bizarre. It’s like he’s handling a overgrown pup. The other immediately brightens, biting every bite Mydei gives him, happily.

Something in Mydei’s chest twists at these small things. This was new to him, to them, being this close to the other. Of course, Phainon would always drag Mydei off to baths, dinners, like it was normal. But he knows how closed off the other is at the same time. To see him so out of his normal zone feels... odd. But comforting.

And Mydei can’t deny the tension between them.

They were equals—and Alphas. So it was normal for them to be competing with each other, right? Phainon would always respect Mydei’s space. He never crossed the line. Never made either of them uncomfortable—well, ignoring what happened today. But that was... semi-conscious.

He looks at Phainon, who takes another bite from the fork he offers, happily smiling. Mydei would’ve smiled too, if it weren’t for that haze clouding the other’s eyes.

This was Phainon’s Alpha, Mydei tells himself. Not entirely Phainon. He needs the other’s consciousness too.

Aglaea’s words rang in his ears,

‘He’s submitting to you.’

That’s... the problem.

When they spar, it doesn’t end until one of them yields. And most of the time, they don’t—until one can’t stand anymore. Heck, they were at each other’s throats for ten days. So yes, they’re both stubborn Alphas.

To think that an Alpha like that gave up so easily to him... This, this is something else.

He needs to talk to Phainon about all of this. Really talk. He will apologize—but not now. They need to sort out these feelings. Right now, the other will just whine, thinking he’s been rejected.

So that’s a talk for later.

Right now, he’ll focus on taking care of him.

Mydei let his hand dip into the water, checking the temperature. They should’ve just gone to the private baths instead of being here. Yet here they were, in Mydei’s own bath, which he rarely used, now filled with hot, comfortable water.

But considering the chances of running into someone he knows or anyone was best avoided. For both his and Phainon’s sake. Mydei sighed as he took his hand away from the bath.

His other hand, however, was occupied.

Occupied with keeping a certain Alpha busy.

Mydei glared at the white haired Alpha beside him, who was currently playing with his right hand. Intertwining fingers, tracing knuckles, caressing each line like he’d never seen Mydei’s bare hands before.

Infuriating, Mydei thought. He was handling a pup. That much he had realized now. His brain just couldn’t process it before. Because never had he imagined the side of the one he considered his equal, an Alpha of great strength, to be so… carefree? Unguarded? Completely bare? He doesn’t even know. And all this in front of him of all people. It was all too shocking, but for now it’s just something he’ll have to deal with.

They were in Mydei’s bath. Their armor off. All the heavy clothing too—well, Phainon’s heavy clothing. Mydei swears there were too many straps on this man. He had to uncover all of them one by one while they stripped. Stripped to just their undergarments.

As soon as his gauntlets were off, and so Phainon found a new hobby, examining Mydei’s bare hands like it was one of the the most deep buried mysteries of Amphoreus.

Mydei shook his head and exhaled a deep sigh, then wordlessly raised the hand in the other’s grasp. Just high enough to align with the other’s face. He let it hover for a bit, and as Phainon glanced up, curious, Mydei just grabbed the poor alpha’s face and shoved him into the water, completely nonchalant. The other landed face first, butt up, knees in the bath before scrambling upright, coughing out water, grabbing the pools’s edge for support as he heaved and pouted toward Mydei. Face red.

Mydei found himself smiling. For the first time.

Now that was a reaction he had recognized—or rather, expected. It made Mydei relax, somewhat. That it wasn’t just some shapeshifter in disguise as his Phainon. So he laughed—laughed his worries away. Laughed like this wasn’t all a cruel joke shoved in his face just to twist with his heart.

Phainon tilted his head, confused as to why the other was laughing. But since Mydei was smiling, Phainon decided to smile too as he leaned over the bath’s edge, resting his head on his hands.

And just like that, some tension between the two eased up. Mydei cleaned both of them, Phainon obviously clinging to him like a lifeline. After they were freshened up, well not fully, but somewhat dressed in leisure chitons, Mydei led them toward his bedroom.

Where his bed was.

With one bed.

A bed big enough for two adults.

And Mydei stopped dead in his tracks.

Phainon knocked his nose into the back of the other’s head, not expecting the abrupt stop. He made a confused noise and looked, rubbing his sore nose. Mydei stood there, completely still, looking fine but a storm clearly running through his mind. Spiraling over sharing a bed for the first time.

So Phainon, most thoughtful Alpha of the moment, stepped in front of Mydei, grabbed his face, and squished his cheeks to get his attention. Mydei’s thoughts cleared instantly to the sight of Phainon, just inches away, holding his face.

His gaze dropped, traitorous eyes scanning the other's lips. Because that’s where a normal person would look if they had a big fat crush—if they were inches apart, breath fanning across their faces. One yank and those lips would be on his—

But Mydei’s instinct and rational mind weren’t on the same page to his own disappointment, as his hand pushed the other away instead of following through with… whatever fantasy he just had.

The other Alpha let himself be pushed, knees hitting the bed's edge, making him sit. He looked up at Mydei.

And Mydei blinked. His eyes traveled over the man sitting on his bed. This may look like the most scandalous situation to anyone who barged in at this moment—two half-naked, well respected, strong healthy Alphas, staring at each other hungrily, eyes trailing over one another like it was a feast.

Mydei’s gaze dropped to the exposed thigh under the white chiton that did a very poor job covering them. Then to the mark on the other’s neck—where Mydei’s Alpha pride secretly rests (he’ll never admit it out loud). Then to Phainon’s hazy gold eyes, with just a small hint of blue left, reminding him this wasn’t entirely Phainon. But he could also feel the same hungry gaze directed at his own exposed chest.

Trying to push whatever his primal desire wanted, Mydei manifested all his remaining willpower to try and be the responsible one.

So he cleared his throat, arms crossing over his chest, a bit self-conscious under the other's gaze.

“You take that side,” he said, pointing to the right side of the bed. “This side is mine.” He glared at the other, who was currently sitting on his side.

Phainon blinked. Dumbly. Then scrambled, wordlessly, toward the right side, settling obediently into place and smiling at Mydei.

Mydei rolled his eyes at the behavior before settling onto his side, tossing the comforter aside.

The moment he hit the mattress, he could feel himself melt into it. Exhausted. Mentally and physically.

Just as his eyes were about to shut down for the day, he felt a small tug from behind.

And Mydei felt a vein almost pop.

really now?

Yet he stayed still. Pretending to sleep, and he felt a weight behind him shift, not too close, surprisingly. Was Phainon’s Alpha finally learning some manners? His tired brain joked. Too exhausted to even scold him, Mydei let the other do whatever.

Only when he felt the other's breathing even out did he finally turn back. Phainon was sleeping on his side, facing him, a hand half reached out like it had stopped mid reach.

It made Mydei almost feel guilty for not holding it.

He turned fully, watching him.

Phainon looked peaceful.

His white hair was a mess. His lashes brushed against his cheeks, eyes closed, breathing soft. The usual tension in his features had vanished and he looked young, almost gentle like this.

Mydei’s gaze drifted to the mark on his neck again. He reached for it unconsciously…then stopped, afraid he’d wake him. He let his hand drop and rested his eyes on Phainon’s face again, watching the peaceful expression. And so he rested his eyes like that, feeling a surprising warmth bloom in his chest.

…

Mydei wakes up with a gasp. He was woken by the sharp pain on his back. As a warrior, his immediate response was alarm, his hands went to grip the threat that was causing him harm.

As he was about to tear the weight and pain or whatever it was off him, he heard a barely audible whimper, and he snapped his eyes open.

It took a second to process and fully grasp the situation as his sleep-alarmed mind cleared.

He was in his room.

And he remembered going to sleep with Phainon.

But he doesn’t remember what caused this position.

He was now on his other side with Phainon under his chin, who was breathing heavily with a arm that had a death grip on his back. He could feel the stinging pain of the other's nails piercing through his skin. And the air around the room smelled like something charred, overripe and with a fading hint of golden musk that screamed anguish.

Confused further, he looked down at Phainon, still asleep with his eyes tightly shut, but nothing in his face said calm. He looked distressed, a color painted across his face that Mydei could recognize as a familiar feeling of a nightmare. The scent was highlighting his distress.

Of course, Mydei himself wasn’t a stranger to nightmares, so he isn’t surprised the other was the same. Phainon, who never truly elaborated about his childhood other than losing his companions and kin—he assumed it must’ve been bad.

He gently nudged the other, trying to wake him up. The other only tightened the grip, making Mydei hiss a bit. He was sure there’d be marks on his back. And Mydei was genuinely too tired to deal with this right now. He needed sleep. They both did. And his mind wasn’t exactly patient right now.

And just like that his own hazy, tired mind took over. He rolled them over, pushing Phainon flat on his back with both hands on the other’s shoulders, hovering over him.

His mind provided only one solution right now. So he buried his nose deep into the other’s neck, inhaling deeply—taking in the full smell of citrus and golden musk. It was almost overtaken by the charred, burnt scent but still there. And he let his nose wander, exploring Phainon’s pale skin, nuzzling in to tracing the curve of his shoulder.

Mydei lets his own scent of smoked sandalwood with a hint of red peppercorn take over, trying to dominate the other’s charred and distressed scent, scenting him openly, trying to wake the other up.

Phainon through the process, somewhat loosened the death grip he had on his back, and makes a quiet noise.

Which meant it was working.

Mydei found himself purring a bit with satisfaction. He could feel the other reveal his neck more, baring it, completely giving in to his touch—Mydei’s lips parted against the neck, mouthing at the skin just above the bite mark. Then dragging his tongue over to the healing mark.

And Phainon moaned, hands sliding up from Mydei’s back to grip his hair. Something inside Mydei buzzed in pride.

The scent of charred, burnt distress dulled back to its normalcy while both of their scents mixed, making Mydei more and more delirious. He found himself unable to resist the sweet smell of blossoming citrus as his nose was suddenly attacked with its full glory. He heard a soft gasp as his tongue dragged with more pressure over the sun tattoo—to almost sucking over it like hungry animal, the white haired alpha had moaned again and his grip on Mydei’s hair trembling—too sensitive to the touch there, his body arched up into him, chest brushing against his own, skin against skin.

Mydei wanted. Titans, he wanted more.

“So good for me,” He praised, kissing his mark. A broken whine answered, one that was needier.

Smirking against the skin, Mydei let’s mouth traveled higher, bolder now, right under the other’s jaw, leaving a soft trail of wet kisses while his nose ghosted over. He felt hot—too hot, and eventually found his way to the other’s ear, licking the skin under it teasingly. That was rewarded with another eager whine.

“So sensitive,” Mydei growled at the discovery, nosing his way to the other’s cheek. There was no distance between them. Mydei was practically on Phainon with his hands now cradling the other’s head, his mouth wandering over his face to his jaw, then back to the neck, hearing more and more pathetic noises from the other, Mydei mouthed the area between Phainon’s jaw and Adam’s apple —a dangerous area. No one should be this exposed, but whatever possessed him now was bold enough to lick that area, let alone on an alpha. To his luck he was allowed. Humming happily, he found his way to the unmarked side.

Phainon eagerly tilted his head, allowing the other Alpha to explore. Mydei, now more than pleased, let his hands roam across the other's torso as he licked and sucked at his neck, humming in satisfaction at a soft whine.

Phainon’s fingers tightened in Mydei’s hair, quiet cries spilling past his lips with every brush of touch over skin no one else had dared to claim.

The urge to sink in his teeth right there, this instant, clouded Mydei’s mind. And those noises of eagerness coming out from the other weren’t helping his hazy mind at all.

He wanted him.

Mydei wanted Phainon.

He wanted him to be his. His only.

He felt himself opening his mouth, baring his teeth—just about to sink them in. mine. To claim what was his. mine, mine, mine To mark. To make—

Mydei stopped. Blinking to clear the blur in his eyes. His vision sharpened, suddenly very awake. He took a few breathes before taking in the sight beneath him.

Phainon was under him.

Phainon was under him…on his bed.

Phainon lay there, head turned to the side, panting heavily. Neck fully bared, slick with Mydei’s saliva, gleaming in the dim light. His dazed, heat hazed gold—with barely any blue left, gazed up at him through heavy lids. His mouth was parted, his face flushed, and Mydei could even see the tears that had pooled along his lashes. He ignored how the Alpha inside him practically roared at the sight.

Mydei’s eyes dropped to his own hands, frozen mid action, one over Phainon’s chest, the other on his hips.

His eyes widened. And panic began to bloom.

What.

What was he—

His mind momentarily blacked out from the sudden panic. Until an impatient Phainon whined, fingers still tangled in his hair, and yanked him back down.

Mydei fell with an "oof" onto the other’s chest. Mind buffering. Just as the panic threatened to fully consume him again, a face nuzzled into his head. Phainon inhaled softly, and suddenly the whole room filled with the scent of fresh citrus and golden dusk. Unnaturally calming,

Mydei felt his body go soft, too soft all the tension easing. And only then did he realize just how exhausted he really was.

And just as his panic—or whatever had happened could fully process, sleep claimed him once more, and he dropped deadweight on top of the other alpha. Exhausted.

…

Mydei woke up to something warm.

Warm—and comfortable in a way that made him want to stay asleep just a bit longer. It radiated heat, grounding him. He would’ve ignored it… if not for the rhythmic thump-thump beneath his ear.

He frowned. What the hell was that?

Blinking open his eyes, he found himself facing the half-open window. The morning breeze gently licked his face. Light filtered in soft gold. And yet, oddly, his view was… moving? Up and down?

Still, none of this explained the warmth beneath him.

Then the warmth shifted. Slightly. Like it was breathing.

Brows furrowing, Mydei flexed his back muscles and pushed himself up, only to realize—he was lying on his chest.

Something he never did.

And just as he was beginning to rise, he looked up and came face to face with a very… smiling, goofy, too-happy for this hour face.

Mydei scowled, eyelids heavy with sleep.

The face looked stupid.

And familiar.

His brain, still fogged from sleep, took a few moments longer than it should’ve. But eventually it clicked: he was practically on top of someone. And that someone was Phainon. Or rather, his chest which was warm, toned, annoyingly comfortable.

He’d spent the night laying on Phainon’s chest.

Without a word, Mydei removed himself from the cozy body heat and rolled off the bed like a disgruntled cat. Standing, he made a straight line to the bathroom—ignoring the soft, whiny noise of protest from the lump still in his bed.

At the sink, he filled a small bowl and splashed cold water on his face—then over his head. The icy shock trailed down his reddish-blond strands to his bare torso, grounding him. Slowly, he opened his eyes to the mirror.

Yet unfortunately, his mind had recorded last night a little too clearly. The image of Phainon beneath him, panting heavily, neck fully bared—

He almost bashed his head into the mirror, feeling the heat rush straight to his abdomen.

He needed a shower.

A cold shower.

A long cold shower.

Mydei felt bothered.

Both of them were currently seated in his kitchen having breakfast, with Mydei offering small pieces of bread toward a certain Phainon, who still didn’t seem to have woken up from the headspace Mydei had accidentally thrown him into.

But that was not what bothered him.

Mydei found himself ripping the next piece of bread a bit too harshly, hating how frustrated he felt. And next to him, Phainon waited to be fed, obediently wagging his imaginary tail excitedly.

And that wasn’t why he was bothered either.

Just a few quints ago—

Mydei had finished his endlessly long shower. He dressed for the day and stepped out of the bathroom—only to be met face to face with a grinning Phainon, who looked like he’d been standing there far too long.

Mydei opened his mouth in disbelief, then shook his head. Trying to ignore the other by walking pass him.

And that’s when it hit him—the scent of smoked sandalwood with a hint of red peppercorn.

His scent.

Mydei’s eyes widened at the realization.

Phainon was reeking of it.

Which clearly explained why the other looked so smug and satisfied. But Mydei was having none of it. His face burned. It was embarrassing—the memories of last night flashing across his vision, overlapping the face in front of him.

Phainon’s unfocused eyes gazing up at him, panting, flushed—

Mydei pinched the bridge of his nose, shutting his eyes to shake off the image.

So even after his own shower, Mydei had taken his time—because he was patient, because he was calm. He’d refilled the bath. All for Phainon. This stupid Alpha, who clearly didn’t function properly in his Subspace, could have a proper soak. And Mydei, who’d accidentally coated the other in too much of his scent could help wash it off.

He also had to carry the overgrown Alpha to the bathroom, simply because the other turned unreasonably uncooperative the second he saw what Mydei intended to do.

Mydei just didn’t understand the fuss. He had stripped Phainon and tried to put him in the water— forcefully, yes—and Phainon scrambled out of the tub like a wet cat allergic to water. And since Mydei had already gotten ready for the day, he had to avoid getting splashed.

Except that was impossible when the other kept thrashing, trying to leap out and escape.

Mydei held him down by the shoulders from behind, guiding him into the shallow pool. But the white haired Alpha still tried to stand up—causing droplets to land on Mydei’s freshly dry clothes.

“Deliverer, stop,” Mydei muttered. Irritated. The other didn’t listen.

So, as you can imagine, this had gotten messy. And to make it even more chaotic, Phainon’s hands reached back to grab at Mydei’s clothes—probably to gain leverage and thrash more easily.

“Stop that,” Mydei winced. Phainon only let out a dissatisfied whine.

Mydei felt his frustration rising. Phainon wasn’t listening. He kept kicking his feet, splashing water everywhere. Every time he resisted, Mydei’s irritation grew—not just because of the mess, but also because the Alpha wasn’t obeying him. Wasn’t letting him take care of him.

And the growl building in his throat finally slipped out.

“Stop fucking struggling and behave.” he snapped before he could stop himself.

The whining Alpha went completely pliant in his grip. Hands that had gripped his clothes retreated and dropped to their own sides, into the water. Legs that had kicked just stopped, folding themselves underneath.

And Mydei blinked at the sudden peace. Thrown off guard.

A few beats passed, and the bathroom went still and quiet, if not for the sound of running water from the tap next to them.

Phainon was quiet. And Mydei began to get worried again.

Because what did he do this time?

So as careful and caring as he could, he asked,

“Hey?” Mydei called out, still behind the other, his hands that were on Phainon’s shoulders now resting on his lap from where he was crouched down. “You okay?” he asked softly, trying not to scare the other more.

Then he laid a gentle hand on the Alpha’s shoulder, feeling him go tense, then relax under his touch.

He then saw Phainon nod. He sighed, relieved—yet he still couldn’t see the other’s face. And so quietly Mydei started to wash him, there was a part of him that screamed something was wrong.

Ignoring everything else, Mydei started washing him from the back, pouring water over him, then moving toward the front, caressing the skin as gently as he could, hoping it would be comforting, and gentle enough.

Just like that, he reached the neck.

He knew that was where most of the scent he had left behind remained. So his hand slowly reached there and touched, warning the other that he was going to start washing there.

But just as Mydei’s hand accidentally touches a bit too high over Phainon’s neck—right under the jaw, something wet touches his knuckles. He frowns. He hadn’t washed the other’s face yet, and there’s no way water could’ve reached his face, seeing Phainon’s hair was still dry.

Confusion bubbling with a hint of concern, Mydei’s hands roamed from his jaw toward the other’s cheek. He still can’t seem to see Phainon’s face fully. But he could feel the other flinch.

Indeed, the other Alpha’s face was wet and hot, which shouldn’t be possible, because the bath itself was cold. Mydei inhales a bit. The bath indeed smelled faintly of something charred and dimming in distress—but it isn’t very prominent that he didn’t even notice before.

“Phainon,” he finds himself calling out, the feeling of something like dread crawling upon him in some form of realization.

And his suspicion is confirmed correctly when he hears a soft sniffle. Barely audible, but there.

“Turn around,” Mydei asks, as gently as he can. He doesn’t want to make this more difficult than it already is.“Please.”

To his relief, the other does. Slowly turns his body enough to come face to face with him.

And Mydei feels his stomach lurch.

The other Alpha was crying.

Or rather Phainon had been crying—silently—all while Mydei didn’t notice or was too busy trying to bath him. To add to that, this was his first time seeing the other cry this openly. His face was flushed and wet, his eyes wide and shimmering. Tears streaked down in silence—not a single sob— just an unrelenting stream that didn’t stop, even after he turned. They slide down his cheeks and drip from his chin. Not much expression on him. He just stares back, looking apologetic.

When Mydei doesn’t say anything, he sniffs again, face twisting into more of a grimace.

“I’m sorry,” Phainon whispers, barely audible.

And Mydei hadn’t heard Phainon speak since yesterday. And when he said “heard,” he meant actual words, not the whines, not the sighs, not the soft noises he made when touched. So this—this was the first word in hours.

And it didn’t make him feel any better.

If anything, it landed like a slap.

He looked at Phainon properly now, taking in his face, the soft blankness of it, the dull shine in his eyes, and the weight of concern hit him all at once. Along with guilt.

He doesn’t like that look.

He wants it gone.

Mydei’s mind was loud.

The urge to comfort him—to wipe that guilty, hollow look off his face, claws at Mydei’s chest. It aches, sharper than it should. His hand is already reaching forward.

Had he hurt him?

He didn’t mean to.

Never.

He would never hurt him.

Never meant to hurt him.

Never wants to see that expression on him.

Never again.

Mydei’s calloused hands find the other’s face, cradling it between his fingers as gently as he can.

Ignoring the hotness of those wet cheeks, his fingers begin to wipe tear after tear from beneath those hazy gold eyes as one by one slip by. Trying to keep them from reaching the rest of his face.

“I’m sorry,” Mydei finds himself saying sincerely. “I’m not mad” The gentleness of his own voice is so foreign to him, but he doesn’t care.

Phainon stares up at him for a bit, before closing his eyes. Nuzzling into the cold hands.

Mydei sighs in relief as he sees the other breathe in, calmness returning, the distressed smell in the room dulling as it happens. But still, the tears wouldn’t stop. Phainon’s lips trembled in his grasp— like he wanted to say something, but couldn’t.

“Tell me what you want,” Mydei says, his voice low—so low that he can feel the other shiver just a little at the sound of it.

He wants to hear it.

He wants to hear it from Phainon.

Even if it’s obvious—Mydei has to hear the other voice it.

He sees the other open his eyes between his palms, cheeks squished, eyes glassy, face wet. His lips parts softly as he whispers,

“You.”

And that was all it took.

Letting go of the face he was holding, Mydei slides into the bath without a care. His clothes cling uncontrollably to him as water soaks through the fabric. Yet he doesn’t care. He just sits down next to Phainon in the pool before opening his arms.

Without any hesitation, the white-headed Alpha crashes into him. Face burying deep into his Alpha’s shoulder, breathing in his scent, calming himself… practically settling himself on top of Mydei’s lap. Mydei can feel the wetness on his bare shoulder but finds himself not minding at all as a small chuckle escapes him. Phainon lets out a high-pitched whine, embarrassed.

Mydei feels the other Alpha’s body shook for a while before it disappears, then practically melts against the hold. Hands wrapped around his neck, still hiding in his shoulder.

“So clingy,” Mydei huffs, burying his nose into the snowy hair, nudging the other a bit.

He only gets a whine in return. Of course.

Mydei shakes his head, kissing the redness of the others ears before returning to clean, even if it means getting himself more soaked in the process. He still proceeds to wash, while the other still rests on his lap.

They get cleaned up. Mydei dresses them both, changing again himself without complaint. He lets Phainon borrow his clothes—slightly loose but brand new and unmistakably his. The red looks off on Phainon’s pale skin, doesn’t quite match the others usual pallet, but Mydei doesn’t care. If anything, something possessive swells in his chest at the sight. His alpha, wrapped in his clothes.

And yet Here they were now.

In his kitchen.

With a very bothered Mydei.

And a clueless Phainon who was staring up at his bread piece being tortured, mouth half open in anticipation.

Mydei twisted the bread in his fingers, watching the crushed bread slowly puff back up to its usual state before throwing it into his own mouth, ignoring the noise the other made in protest.

Whatever, he thinks as he breaks off another piece before shoving it at Phainon’s mouth to shut him up.

As you can see, he was bothered.

And what bothered him more was the reason why he was bothered.

So he had gotten them both out of baths, fully cleaned, and gotten them dry and dressed in comfortable clothes. His clothes, completely normal. Nothing to be bothered about at all.

But the moment Phainon stopped smelling like smoked sandalwood…it affected him more than he’d like to admit.

Yes, the clothes were his. Technically. But they were brand new, untouched by wear, unworn by him. They didn’t carry his scent.

And that… that made him feel strangely restless. Uneasy in a way he couldn’t quite name. And that feeling kept nagging in side of his brain.

And so here he was, expressing his frustration on the poor bread.

Now that he thinks about it, it’s almost funny. Before, it was Phainon who was affected by this. But why is he so affected when he was the one who wanted this… Had his stupid crus-favoritism gone that far.

Throughout all of this, one thing Mydei had realized was he cared for Phainon. More than he had thought before. That he strangely liked the devoted attention he was getting, by this Phainon.

It just confuses him. He adores Phainon as his equal, his rival, his partner, a soldier on the battlefield. He finds time for their spars and looks forward to them, just so he can have that moment of heat—of them losing to their roughness and strength when they’re head to head. When they bicker over the smallest disagreements, one’s rude and pushes snarky comments, the other just matches him perfectly. He admits he likes that. He likes they oppose each other. He likes that they fight.

But why was he liking this too?

These tender, almost fragile moments, with Phainon who’s completely surrendered himself to him.

Mydei’s alpha clawed at him ‘We conquered him.’ No, they didn’t. ‘He’s ours.’ No, he isn’t.

This—

This felt strange.

And wrong.

But he does want it.

He wants this too.

A part of him does.

It’s so perfectly molded into Phainon that Mydei can’t believe what his emotions are saying. It’s all confusing. He knows what he wants—and doesn’t know at the same time.

Mydei looks at his Phainon.

Who’s waiting there for another bite of bread. Big eyes blinking up at him and the bread, while a smile spread across his face. Looking exactly like the normal Phainon when it comes to food. The eyes just throw him off…that’s the problem. Other than that, nothing here says it isn’t normal. It had always been Phainon.

It’s just…

Mydei finds himself asking before he could stop himself, breaking off another piece of bread, “Are you… okay with any of this?”

Even though it’s fruitless and just an attempt to make himself feel better about this whole thing somehow. He still asked. Deep down, maybe he just didn’t want to be rejected.

Phainon tilts his head at the question. Not understanding where it’s coming from. Oblivious.

Mydei can feel his face fall a bit as he offers the bread, hand hanging midair, waiting for the other to take it.

To his surprise, Phainon stands up from where he sat abruptly, then makes himself comfortable in Mydei’s lap—uninvited. Mydei doesn’t protest. Just lets him. But startled nevertheless.

The other Alpha's hand, wordlessly reaches to take the bread piece he’d been offered, then takes it over to Mydei’s closed mouth.

Waiting for it to open.

And so Mydei does not put much thought to it, and Phainon happily feeds the piece to him then wraps his arms around him—cuddling with absolutely no regard for personal space. He clings, practically climbing onto him, legs wrapped around Mydei’s waist, face buried in his broad shoulder.

Mydei exhales, arms circling around the other’s frame, one hand reaching up to gently pet his hair.

The question felt answered, in a way.

Somewhere in Mydei's quatres, his teleslate buzzed with a urgent message.

Chapter End Notes
