Mydei was never the type to show public affection. He wasn’t the kind to hug, shake hands, or— Titan forbid—touch anyone in front of watchful eyes. It wasn’t disgust, nor ignorance of courtship. No. He simply never saw the point in wasting time with meaningless skinship. To him, touch was a weapon, a language reserved for battles and war. Nothing more.

Outside of that, he was an Alpha who kept his hands to himself. They either folded across his chest or hung at his sides, rigid and steady. He liked his space. He guarded it. Everyone around him knew this well—especially the other Heirs. And they respected it.

Which is why he understood the stares. Why he could feel them drilling into him from every corner of the Twilight Courtyard.

For instance, Castorise—her jaw slack, openly gawking in what could only be described as awe, for some titan-damned reason leaning closer to Hyacine as though needing confirmation that this was really happening. Cifera lingered in the shadows like a restless wildcat, but even she had tilted her head, eyes sharp and curious on him. And Aglaea… Aglaea watched him with that unnervingly knowing look. A look that said she understood. That she saw too much.

The stares themselves weren’t surprising. Mydei expected them. What he hadn’t expected was the burning in his ears, the creeping heat rising to his face, or the way his grip—unthinking, unrelenting—tightened around the hand he was holding.

Yes. The undying crown prince, Mydeimos of Kremnos, son of Gorgo—now stood in the center of Twilight Courtyard, face burning like a chastised groveboy, while his hand remained firmly intertwined with their Deliverer.

Phainon, of course, looked like he didn’t have a single care in the world. Broad grin on his face, shoulders loose, standing there as if the scene wasn’t making the entire room silently combust with implications. Still in his own little subspace, still oblivious—or worse, pretending to be oblivious— to the many, many conclusions everyone in this room was no doubt drawing.

It had all started the moment Aglaea summoned him on such short notice. Duty had called, and he had wasted no time in answering. Well—almost no time.

He had made one detour.

Straight to Phainon’s quarters.

Which, in hindsight, had been a mistake. Or at least not the smartest idea. Because what should have been a swift “fetch and go” became… something else. Dressing Phainon…of all was an impossible task and had eaten up precious time. Mydei had insisted on it, though. The white-haired alpha had been half-wrapped in attire with aesthetically unmatching red and golds(Mydei’s own), looking nowhere near considerable to be presented before the heirs. So Mydei ever so kindly had stripped him out of it, tugging him into something decent. His own clothes, to be precise. Usual dark shirt that fit, trousers and boots.

The outer coat he abandoned halfway through. Too many buckles. Too many straps. He didn’t have the patience and time.

And the choker. He hadn’t forgotten that. He had fished through Phainon’s wardrobe and grabbed the first leather one he could find, fastening it around his neck—high enough to hide the mark he’d left there. He had ignored the frankly concerning number of chokers in that closet. Didn’t even want to question it.

Not that any of it mattered in the end, because seconds later he’d had Phainon shoved against the wall, face buried in his neck and collar, scenting him until the other alpha’s knees nearly buckled—

The point was, he had still made it here. He had still barged into the Courtyard as normally as he could, dragging along their Deliverer who looked presentable enough, and—most importantly—in one piece.

Now, though, with every eye fixed on them, Mydei could feel the tips of his hair matching the flush across his face. Crimson, hot, impossible to disguise.

The stares didn’t falter for some time.

Until Aglaea cleared her throat—sharp enough to slice through the silence.

“I truly apologize for calling you at such short notice,” she began, her tone formal, steady. “But unfortunately, a new threat plagues our city, and I need all of your attention on this case.”

Her gaze shifted. It landed firmly, almost accusingly, on the Kremnoen Prince. “Especially you, Mydeimos.”

Mydei hadn’t been addressed so directly, so pointedly—by Aglaea in a long while. Not even after the incident yesterday. She was choosing to ignore it, then. Though there was a flicker of something…an apology, perhaps when her eyes brushed past him and Phainon.

Then it clicked.

Nothing would make her call him out this openly, under these circumstances… unless—

“It is a matter involving a Kremnoen,” Aglaea confirmed aloud, almost reading the thought off his face. “An Alpha.”

The words landed heavy. She turned, gesturing for Mydei to follow.

He did. His boots trailed after the Goldweaver’s light steps as she led him to a closed-off wing, unlocking the door with a quiet click.

The moment the door opened, the smell hit him.

A scent of an Omega in heat.

Sharp, cloying, and impossible to mistake. Mydei stopped at the threshold, shoulders going rigid. Aglaea entered without hesitation, but she spared him a brief glance over her shoulder— understanding, but not demanding.

He wouldn’t be affected, no. His control was iron. But stepping inside meant intrusion, offense, violation of an Omega’s vulnerability. That was something he would not do. He stayed by the door.

Phainon, though, had already stiffened beside him at the scent. Not badly—but enough. Mydei shifted subtly, keeping his body angled in front, shielding him from the sight within the room. His hand found Phainon’s, thumb brushing circles into pale knuckles, grounding him.

The other Alpha heir looked tense, confused, but still held himself together. Better than Mydei expected, considering the haze of subspace that still lingered over him. If anyone else had noticed, there might have been whispers. But Aglaea only carried on, unbothered.

What a dangerous woman, Mydei thought. To know their limits so well. To calculate outcomes before they even moved. She acted as though she knew them more intimately than they knew themselves. Dangerous—and frightening.

Still, he kept his distance. From the doorway, he observed.

The woman lying on the infirmary bed looked Okheman from her features, her crumpled attire confirming it. She was unconscious, her brow twisted faintly in pain. The scent-blockers Hyacine might’ve applied clung thick to her skin, masking the worst of it—but not enough. It was obvious. She was in heat.

Mydei frowned. His mind was already weighing questions—why here? why her? why involve them at all?

Before he could ask, movement stirred inside the room.

Anaxa emerged.

He looked as though he’d been waiting for the first excuse to leave, expression bored as ever. A cloth covered the lower half of his face, no doubt to dull the scent. The omega professor’s voice sharp with irritation.

“What is wrong with you, woman?” he snapped, not even waiting for introductions. “You bring two Alpha heirs to a room like this?”

His eyes flicked toward the threshold—and froze.

Mydei and Phainon stood side by side, close enough that their joined hands were obvious. Mydei’s thumb still idly circling. His posture protective, deliberate. And Phainon pale and tense behind him.

Anaxa blinked once. His face twisted. A mix of fascination—and disgust before he scoffed under his breath. Shaking his head. He said nothing else, he turned his back, his coat sweeping behind him as he strode away.

Aglaea, who had only watched with the faintest of smiles, ignored the tension in the room. As if none of it had happened. She stepped forward, her tone even, almost too casual.

“This omega woman is a victim of the Kremnoen we spoke of earlier,” she began, moving closer to the bed. Her hand rested lightly on the damp forehead of the distressed figure. At her touch, the woman’s shaking eased, if only a little.

Aglaea’s voice lowered. “The worst of it is this: she wasn’t born an omega. She was a beta. Just days ago, her family reported her missing. Cifera found her soon after, but by then…” She paused, her fingers brushing damp hair back from the woman’s temple. “By then she had already shifted. Forced into a secondary gender she was never meant to have.”

The silence that followed was heavy, pressing against the walls.

“It was no natural turn,” Aglaea continued, her eyes moving over the gathered heirs before settling on Mydei. “The Alpha who fled the scene left behind more than one broken body. This one survived. Others were not so fortunate. Some were even Alphas themselves.”

Mydei leaned forward with an arched brow. “An Alpha, drugged? That’s… not easy to manage.”

“Indeed,” Aglaea said. “Which means what we’re dealing with is not ordinary.” She straightened, her tone sharpening as though to cut through the disbelief. “It is a drug. A highly modified rut–heat compound. Potent enough to trigger a cycle even in those who were never meant to experience one. Potent enough to drag a beta into another gender altogether.”

Mydei’s throat worked as he swallowed, his voice quieter, sardonic in the way it always was when he wanted to mask unease. “So not just cruel, but...”

“Efficient,” Aglaea corrected grimly. “It’s been circulating for some time. Sold, traded, distributed in shadows. The suspect behind it has been confirmed as a Kremnoen—a fleeting one. Which makes them slippery. Cifera tracked the trail, but it broke.”

The cat-girl, leaning against the walls just near the door frame, flicked her tail with irritation. “He knows how to vanish. No footprints. No scent. Nothing. It’s like chasing smoke.”

Aglaea’s hand lingered on the victim’s forehead a moment longer before she finally withdrew, her eyes darkening. “But he cannot run forever. Not from us.”

Mydei had asked if there were any clues, his hand still firmly holding Phainon’s as though the two of them were a single piece.

Aglaea shook her head. “Nothing concrete. A scar under an eye and that he’s Kremnoen. Middle-aged. Alpha. The accent gives it away though”  Her tone was even, but the weight of the words left the room heavier than before.

Eventually, they were excused to leave. Mydei politely left, taking Phainon with him before Aglaea could elaborate further on their possible inconvenience to others.

The moment they stepped outside, something like shame clutched at his chest. His own blood, his own people—Kremnoen, of all names—tied to this. They were known to stay clear of such filth, a standard he had upheld fiercely, ensuring none in their ranks gave reason for suspicion. Yet one had slipped beneath his notice, hiding for who knew how long. And now there were victims. More victims. Each thought weighed heavier, pressing him further into silence as they walked.

He was so caught in the spiral of it that he didn’t notice Phainon had slowed, then stopped altogether—until the grip on his hand tightened back, tugging him to a halt. He made a faint, confused sound, turning his head to question him—only to find Phainon’s attention fixed elsewhere.

Not on him.

But on a restaurant across the corner, its lantern-light spilling warm and golden onto the street. Phainon stood there staring at it like a child spotting sweets in a market, eyes locked on the store with a kind of single-minded hunger. Then, inevitably, his stomach growled loud enough to be heard.

Mydei blinked. And when Phainon blinked back at him, almost sheepish, waiting as like asking for permission…he could only stare back with raised brow. Of course. Even at this hour, this man was hungry. Of course.

He exhaled sharply through his nose, shaking his head in endear—disbelief. And then he nodded.

Phainon beamed instantly, beyond happy, before tugging him toward the restaurant without hesitation.

Mydei let himself be dragged. Somewhere in the back of his mind, he had already given up on any restraint where Phainon was concerned. Better this than then encountering a situation like today morning.

So the thoughts of Kremnoen, of failure and shame, bled away, leaving him only with the ridiculousness of the present. His focus shifted entirely, helplessly, to the Alpha pulling him along like a spoiled heir eager for his favorite treat. And Mydei, for all his composure, followed— ignoring the curious stares, the hushed whispers of passing citizens that trailed after.

He ignored them because he chose to. Because he had already decided, whatever others saw, however absurd it might look—he would allow himself this. Allow himself to be dragged along, tethered to Phainon’s whims, no matter how foolish it seemed.

And in the privacy of his own silence, he bit his cheek to keep from smiling.

Because the truth was simple, and damning: he was terribly weak when it came to this particular person.

“Ah, Lord Phainon, Lord Mydei,” a middle-aged beta woman, Eleni greeted warmly when they stepped inside. “Welcome.”

Mydei gave her a polite nod. He’d been here before, dragged along more times than he could count. One of Phainon’s favorite haunts. Usually, the white-haired Alpha would sweep in with that blinding grin, charming greetings spilling out like a showman on stage.

Not today.

Today, Phainon only blinked at the woman… then promptly turned his blank stare onto Mydei, like a man who’d forgotten how to speak.

The woman’s brows pinched with concern.

Mydei, quick on his feet, cleared his throat and covered in smoothly,“Don’t mind him. The Deliverer’s off duty today—lost a bet, sulking. Tired, that’s all.” A lie delivered with perfect courtesy.

At his side, Phainon nearly let out a pathetic little sound—Mydei’s boot stomped discreetly on his foot before it could escape. The Alpha’s eyes almost watered, and Mydei pretended nothing happened.

“Ah, poor soul,” the woman murmured with sympathy. “Shall I prepare your usual private room?”

“Yes. Thank you,” Mydei answered smoothly.

While they waited, a young couple entered, a tall Alpha and his heavily pregnant Omega. Both offered polite greetings towards them before moving to a table nearby.

Mydei told himself not to look too long. And failed.

The Alpha pulled out a chair, helping his mate ease down with tender care. The Omega’s grateful smile lingered as he settled. Simple. Ordinary. A sight Mydei had never spared a thought for before.

But the image lodged itself in his mind anyway—Phainon, pregnant and heavy with his pups, Mydei fussing over him with ridiculous, endless love—

What.

In a attempt to not smash his head hard to the nearest wall or table, Mydei’s grip on Phainon’s hand tightened hard enough to make the other wince. A half-strangled yelp escaped Phainon before he twisted toward him in confusion. His hazy gaze tracked the line of his Alpha’s eyes… and landed on the mated Omega across the room.

An Omega.

His Alpha was staring at…an Omega. That was all Phainon’s dazed, possessive brain processed.

Normally, Rational, conscious, non-hazed Phainon would look at this scene, swallow his annoying feelings, and make a joke at Mydei for staring at omegas like a helpless, brute romantic—or jab him while batting his eyes or winking like a bro.

Nope.

Whatever self-control Phainon had, his Alpha did not. Because who the fuck steals his Alpha’s attention away from him? When he shook Mydei’s hand, the other looked like he was fighting his inner demons or something, which again, processed wrong in the hazed white-haired mind.

So slightly irritated, Phainon just leaned in and bit his Alpha’s bare shoulder. It wasn’t harsh, but it was enough to sting.

The effect was immediate. Mydei’s head snapped around so fast it nearly cracked.

And there was Phainon, smiling sweetly now that he had his Alpha’s full attention, draping an arm around his waist like he belonged there.

Publicly.

In full view.

A mating gesture.

The timing couldn’t be worse—the owner was just returning, calling that their room was ready— when Mydei acted fast. His hand shot up, clamping Phainon around the shoulders and neck in what could pass as a competitive Alpha headlock.

To everyone else, playful roughhousing. To him, a desperate damage-control maneuver. The Alpha in his arms grunted, struggling against the hold. Mydei didn’t care. Not right now.

“Excuse us,” Mydei told the woman calmly, dragging Phainon toward their private room without another word.

The woman only gave them a confused little look, but said nothing. To her, this was simply their usual… dynamic.

Mydei was so tired. The exhaustion he felt weighed on him both mentally and physically. There was a rogue Alpha among his people, a dangerous drug that might threaten countless lives—both his and many others’. The fragile peace they had just been enjoying could be shattered at any moment. And then there was Phainon, the Deliverer, acting as if they were a mated pair, oblivious to it all, as if nothing else in the world mattered at all right now. The Deliverer he had known for years, revealing some parts of himself that he had never even imagined before. And then there were his own confused, mixed feelings. He had, in some measure, accepted Phainon’s overly aggressive devotion, which had seemingly appeared from nowhere. That he’s so surprised how well he handled it all. Well mostly.

He was just so exhausted. Usually, he wouldn’t mind pressure and stress, beating up Phainon in sparring— blowing off steam was an option…but right now it wasn’t and all that felt too much— especially these complicated emotions.

Maybe that was why Mydei had the Deliverer sprawled across his lap, back pressed against his bare chest. His nose was buried deep into the other’s scent glad, inhaling the calming aroma. One hand pressed possessively over the toned lower stomach, the dark shirt slightly lifted to expose skin to his touch. The other hand held Phainon’s mid-air, as if restraining him—not that there’d needed any restraining.

The food they had ordered sat forgotten on the nearby table. Cold.

The booth smelled strongly of Mydei’s smoked sandalwood, dominating the other scents, while his own nose was the only thing accessing Phainon’s.

Phainon was indeed sweeter-smelling than most Alphas Mydei had encountered or been with. The latter had always been insecure about the hint of sweetness in his own scent, but Mydei thought otherwise. The golden musk was strong, but the subtle citrusy sweetness was what he craved. It made his stomach bloom with warmth, somehow calming and grounding him, almost making him want to taste it.

He could feel the other arching against him when his mouth brushed lightly over the sun tattoo. A low, growl slipped past him while the man in his lap made a needy noise.

Mydei didn’t even know how it led to this. All he remembered was getting inside the booth, sitting down, getting their orders, and somewhat feeding Phainon along the way while he ate himself. Somewhere along the line, a small crumb had been left on the side of his mouth, too insignificant for him to notice amidst everything else. He wasn’t even bothered by it, until Phainon leaned in.

Phainon had leaned so close, half on his lap, that Mydei forgot to breathe.

Their faces were inches apart, breaths mingling. His mind was slow, but Phainon closed the distance in an instant, pressing his lips to the side of Mydei’s mouth without care, licking the crumb off sweetly before returning to his original position—still half on his lap. Mydei’s brain nearly shut down, thirty-three million gears turning, trying to process what had just happened. It wasn’t a kiss. No. But it was. And Mydei’s tired brain and weak heart were too furious to let it slide, because the next thing he knew, he had manhandled the other with so much frustration.

Which was how they ended up like this.

Not that Mydei’s tired brain had registered fully on what he was doing so publicly. The owner could barge in at any moment and witness all of it. His rational mind did acknowledged this from somewhere deep inside.

Yet no. He wanted to be greedy for a moment. He wanted to be selfish. He wanted to have this feeling entirely for himself. He wanted to forget everything and just stay like this forever, away from prying eyes, away from the weight of the world, just here, like this, with his Phainon.

Mydei’s tongue licked his mark over the sun tattoo. Leather strap that wrapped there before had torn and thrown somewhere during the process. The mark on Phainon’s neck was almost healed— curse the other’s quick healing abilities. Better than an average human. Sooner or later, the man would wake up and everything would return to their usual routine. Phainon might not even remember properly, while Mydei would be left burdened with the memory, forced to act as if it had all been fine.

His teeth nearly grazed the soft porcelain skin at the thought, but he was careful, pinching with his lips rather than biting. The other bolted slightly, and Mydei purred, lifting his face from the neck toward the other’s ear, mouthing at the ear lobe. He heard the whine he had expected.

The hand pressing over the stomach shifted slightly, feeling the other’s breath shudder while the soft skin spasmed subtly. The touch was new. Mydei found himself rubbing in circles absentmindedly while nuzzling the back of Phainon’s head, white hair brushing his face.

His mind wondered back to previous thoughts as he touched the flat abdomen—imagining Phainon carrying his pups. He was no fool; he knew an Alpha could never carry children. But that didn’t mean he couldn’t pretend, couldn’t try—He pressed firmly on the stomach, his mind too hazy to even question reality, making Phainon whimper out pathetically. Like he could read Mydei’s dark fantasies.

Smiling to himself, Mydei’s nose wandered back towards the other Alpha’s scent glad, until—

Smash.

A loud, alarming clash ripped through their session. Mydei had to tear himself away from the haze to even register what the sound meant. Blinking, he was on his feet the moment his eyes cleared, setting the now distressed man down before rushing outside—barely giving himself a heartbeat to think.

The sound had been unmistakable. A chair being thrown. That was confirmed the second he stepped into the open and spotted the broken remains just a few feet away. His gaze swept quickly, registering the scene.

The restaurant owner was pressed against the wall, pale and frozen. The whole restaurant had erupted into chaos, the handful of customers fleeing. Only three figures remained now—the couple from earlier, and a newcomer.

An Alpha, by the stance of him. The brute had one hand locked around the collar of the mated Alpha, lifting him clean off the ground with inhuman strength. The omega was on their knees, wrecked with panic, eyes wide with horror as their mate struggled against the iron grip.

Mydei moved to intervene—but stopped dead in his tracks when the conversation carried over to him. He didn’t catch all of it. Only a word. One word that mattered.

“…the DRUG, you fool.” The accent was unmistakable. He’d have known it anywhere. That precise lilt, that familiar difficulty with certain syllables—he’d spoken like that himself during his earliest years here. Even dressed carefully in Okehman attire, the man couldn’t fool him.

Kremnoen. One of his. The situation was heated—too heated—but Mydei ducked into the shadows at the edge of the room, choosing to just observe. His jaw was tight, his hands loose at his sides.

“I—I don’t have a-any left!” the struggling Alpha gasped. “Please, you have to understand—” He didn’t finish. The Kremnoen Alpha snarled, shoving him hard to the ground. His gray-and-dark hair fell messily into his face as he dragged a frustrated hand over it, then spat a curse in Kremnoen before laying into the man with vicious kicks.

The omega’s cry was gutting, tearing out of him as he collapsed beside his mate, body curling up, sobbing openly. He reached with trembling hands, desperate to shield his Alpha even as the blows rained down.

That was enough.

Fuck it.

Mydei emerged from the shadows.

The room stilled instantly. The brute’s assault stopped dead, every sense in the space pulled taut as though the air itself had gone razor-thin. Mydei didn’t need to say a word. He stepped forward with calculated calm, every inch of him seething presence, his body a wall between the exit and the others.

The Alpha froze and went pale.

Mydei’s eyes narrowed, cold and unwelcoming. The growl rumbling in his chest carried more weight than a scream. What an insult this man was to his people.

The brute began backing away—slow, cautious—but Mydei was already turning his attention elsewhere. The injured Alpha on the ground was curled on the ground, coughing hard, clutching at his sides.

“Get him to the side,” Mydei ordered the omega, his voice a low, calm fury. “And do not dare leave.”

The omega nodded through trembling lips and half-dragged, half-held his mate away. The shop owner hurried to usher them to a safer corner, where both collapsed into a pile of shock and relief. Only then did Mydei refocus on the Kremnoen.

“Your name.” He didn’t ask. He demanded.

The Alpha trembled where he stood. The scent alone—the raw, thunderous presence of the Kremnoen crown prince was more than enough to crush lesser men. Still, the fool’s eyes darted around, hunting for an opening, a way out.

No answer.

Mydei’s frown deepened. His long stride carried him forward, hand snapping out to seize the man’s face, iron-hard fingers forcing his chin up until their eyes locked. The weaker Alpha shook under the grip, whether from the hold itself or from pure terror.

“Did I not make myself clear?” Mydei spat, voice sharp, dangerous. The man sputtered, words catching in his throat—almost spilling his name, yet choking it back, still clinging to that useless resistance. His hands, trembling but bold enough, reached for Mydei’s side, clawing desperately at the fabric.

That earned another growl. But not from Mydei.

From across the room.

Phainon.

Mydei hadn’t even registered his presence—his shadow had trailed him in silently. The Alpha hadn’t interfered, keeping distance as if not wanting to interrupt Mydei’s pray. But the touch on Mydei’s side, the struggling hands…that had been too much. The sound had slipped from him regardless.

Mydei ignored it. His focus stayed locked on the trembling Alpha in his grip. Scar under the eye. Heavy accent. The description fit. Perfectly. Exactly as the culprit Chiper had been hunting.

“Speak, chorikós,” Mydei hissed, patience bleeding thin.

The man shuddered.

But instead of obedience, his lips twisted into a weak smirk. His gaze flicked back and forth, feigning control where there was none.

“My prince,” he said at last in Kremnoen—sly, but trembling all the same. “Oh, was I interrupting your—“ Then the man asks his eyes flicking briefly toward the white-haired Alpha. Before mouthing “date”

Mydei felt his eye twitch, he really wanted to shove the man’s mouth on to the ground. Where it belonged. Though he held his own. To show provocation wouldn’t work. Not like this.

But the man in his hold saw the faltering. He smirked, growing bolder.

“Is that why your dog is growling at me?” he sneered, tightening his grip on the hand that still had a dead lock on his face.

Mydei shouldn’t let the provocation reach him—he really shouldn’t. Yet the moment Phainon was dragged into it, the restraint somewhat snapped.

The next thing he knew, the Alpha’s jaw broke under his hand.

Gasps echoed from somewhere in the room.

No one dared step in.

And the man, bloodied and terrified, still refused to surrender. He spat some blood onto the floor before fishing something from his clothes. Mydei lunged to stop him, but the man slashed his arm with his hands. Small scratch that resulted a small wound. The wound wasn’t much, he’d heal. But it was enough to make Phainon snarl, angry and feral.

And Mydei—just for a second, got distracted.

His head turned slightly to look at the other in concern.

Too distracted.

The next moment something liquid splattered across his eyes. His grip faltered as he reeled back, covering his face. The man tried to flee.

But he didn’t get far.

A terrifying, furious Deliverer, uncanny to his usual self—slammed him to the ground, pinning him hard, restraining him as if he’d tear him apart. The room held its breath while Mydei clawed at his own vision, trying to clear it.

The second his vision cleared, after blinking away the spots, Mydei saw the struggling man pinned under Phainon. A mix of relief and fury surged through him—glad that Phainon had the upper hand, furious that the situation had spiraled this far.

He blinked harder, trying to clear his vision completely, then moved to step forward, intent on helping Phainon restrain the man. But the Kremnoen was proving more difficult than expected. Even though Phainon was stronger, his mind was hazed—too many openings, too much reckless focus. And the other Alpha saw the chance right there.

Then, before Mydei could even react, the bastard launched upward and though the broken jaw, stubbornly sank his teeth deep into Phainon’s neck.

Mydei felt his heart stop.

He see’s the way Phainon’s eyes widened, shifting from shock to struggle… then faltering, going pliant over the Alpha’s strength.

No.

No no no no.

Not again.

Mydei’s heart hammered loud enough to drown out the world, pumping against his ribs, roaring in his ears. His own Alpha threatened to burst free right then.

He saw red. His jaw clenched so tight it hurt, teeth bared like he was seconds away from tearing the man apart. Rage was spilling into every muscle, into every bone.

He almost lost it.

He almost lashed out on the man outright.

But then—before he could’ve striked, the said man screamed. A sound of pure brutality.

Mydei jerked to the side to see what had happened, and what he saw made him stop cold.

Phainon.

His eyes were narrowed into molten gold, burning with a fury Mydei had never once seen in him before. His teeth bared in animalistic rage, claws sinking deep and ripping across the man’s face without mercy. Blood sprayed. His leg pressed hard against the Alpha’s ribs, crushing down with sickening cracks. The sound made the room wince, made Mydei’s stomach turn—but he couldn’t look away.

Because the Alpha before him wasn’t just angry.

He was feral.

His larger figure loomed over the Kremnoen’s desperate flailing, shoving him down with sheer brutality. The man’s face was twisted, his body snapping forward and down. He had no chance.

And Mydei, through the shock and fury…could only watch in awe.

So this is what Goldweaver meant by ‘Biting his head off’

Literally.

Oh.

Oh.

Soon enough, the man went limp. Terror and pain broke him first, and then unconsciousness. His body sagged against the marble floor like discarded trash.

Above him, Phainon stood hunched over, chest heaving, blood dripping from his claws. His fingers twitched like he didn’t know whether to grab or strike again. Blank, wild-eyed, trembling. The sight wasn’t pleasant to anyone in the room, it was chilling. Mydei knew the three present somewhere in the room, who’d dared watch their Deliverer in such a state, were beyond terrified now.

And the Deliverer himself… Mydei was certain he’d regret what he’d just did apon waking, even if he had no control over it.

Taking a breath, Mydei forced himself to steady. He approached slowly and measured, cautious, as though nearing a wounded, cornered beast. Because that’s what Phainon was right now, not in control, but wild and raw, a beast caught in their instincts.

“Phai,” Mydei said quietly. He wasn’t even sure what to call him to reach through the haze.

But the head turned.

Phainon looked hollowed out. His wide, golden eyes stared through him, and that ugly mark bleeding along his collarbone, beads of gold dripping with it.

That bastard.

He’ll deal with that later.

Mydei extended a hand. Careful and caring. He saw the hesitation flicker across Phainon—his fingers twitching, his entire body caught in a fight-or-flight snap.

But the second he caught Mydei’s scent, Phainon moved. He lunged.

Not to attack, but to cling.

Mydei braced himself for the worst, ready to be clawed or shoved, but instead, Phainon collapsed into him. Hands gripped tight, his entire body throwing itself forward for comfort, for anchor, burying his face into Mydei’s shoulder as if he hadn’t just mauled another Alpha into unconsciousness.

Gasps rippled around the room, but Mydei didn’t care. He caught him, steadying his weight.

He hugged him back.

And despite everything, Phainon—the blood, the brutality—the terror…Mydei couldn’t stop the small smile that crept onto his lips.

Because honestly?

He was kind of cute.

Chapter End Notes

Well Mydei, you sure found wrongest moment to think Phainon was cute…

Anyhow

Chapter Summary

Hyacine needs a break, Mydei needs a break and Phainon needs to wake.

Chapter Notes

Hello!

Here’s another short one!

And might be ooc on some parts for comedic crack reasons!

Enjoy!

Hyacine wouldn’t call today one of the worst days she ever had. No. She has had far more worse days then this. Even so, she had to admit—it had been quite eventful.

The beta-turned-omega had been brought in such a rush that she didn’t even properly hear the full story, too busy staring at the distressed omega who looked to be in far greater pain than a regular omega in heat—until Cipher smacked her with her tail, snapping her out of whatever thoughts had been lingering in her head.

“Snap outta it, kid. She needs painkillers,” Cipher had muttered before disappearing again.

And after that, everything unfolded so fast it blurred into a haze. One moment she was treating the patient, taking blood samples, and the next—Anaxa barged in without a hint of grace, shooing her and her staff out of the room. Very unkind, yet so like her mentor that she found herself waiting outside, questions piling in her head, while he did… well, whatever it was the omega professor had in mind for that poor woman.

One moment she was here, the next she was there, conducting tests and before she could even properly process that, she was summoned into a room full of the other Heirs.

And eventually, her day finally began to crawl toward an end. Well—not truly an end. But she allowed herself a pause, a brief break, after the sheer exhaustion she’d endured from Anaxagoras’ diagnosis and, of course, his experiments.

And so she found herself outside at last, in the courtyard, with little Ica gently pressing a cold water bottle against her face. Hyacine made a soft noise at the chill, but smiled at Ica—tired, yet warm— as she took the bottle. She took a small sip, then sank down onto a nearby bench, leaning back into it, head tilted toward the sky.

So many questions lingered. Curiosity pulled at her, but it was mixed with a heaviness, a sadness, at the possibility that a looming threat might begin to spread, one that could endanger the health of countless innocent lives. The drug was so powerful it was remarkable that any ordinary person could even survive it. There was still so much to uncover—its composition, its origins, the true nature of what it was made from.

The healer omega stretched her legs in quiet frustration. Little Ica shuffled closer, cuddling against her in a small, earnest attempt to comfort. Hyacine let out a slow breath and wrapped her arms around the little guy. They stayed there like that, sitting in a silence that was comfortable, steady.

It was almost curtain-fall hour when her peace broke. The sharp buzz of her teleslate rattled through the courtyard. No doubt another medical emergency concerning the omega still under treatment. But when Hyacine looked at the screen, what she read made her brow furrow, confusion and worry rooting deep in her chest.

When Hyacine arrived at the scene, Okheman soldiers were already stationed at the entrance of the restaurant. A restless crowd had gathered outside, their anxious murmurs spilling into the street, the air thick with the tension of whatever chaos lingered inside.

She hurried in as the guards stepped aside to let her pass, and at once she was struck by the heavy stench of metal… well blood. The sharp tang made her wrinkle her nose as her gaze swept over the room. Her eyes immediately caught the sight of three figures cornered by jagged red crystals. Her frown deepened, but it was the bloodied man on the floor—flanked by two guards, that drew her in.

Hyacine gasped at the sheer brutality left upon his body. Her experienced eyes traced the carnage: his face bore gruesome lacerations, ripped open, skin shredded in grotesque streaks. His eyes were rolled white, pupils nowhere in sight, his mouth frozen open mid-cry—shock carved into his expression as surely as the wounds on his face.

She muttered under her breath as she dropped to her knees, fingers quickly pressing against the man’s throat. Her hand trembled for a moment before she found it—a faint, faltering pulse, fragile but there. Relief escaped her in a sharp exhale, but she wasted no time. Her hands lit with practiced movements, weaving healing into flesh, into bone, enough to stabilize him.

Once she was certain he would not die on the floor, she hurried an order to the soldiers: “Take him to the courtyard.” They obeyed, hoisting the broken man away. Only then did Hyacine allow her attention to shift to the ones—duo she had been deliberately ignoring until now.

Carefully, cautiously, she approached.

Mydei, the Undying Prince. An Alpha untouchable, unshaken, never seen faltering before anyone —now sat on the floor stripped of his usual regal poise. His golden eyes were open, yet glazed, unfocused, as though he was caught somewhere between exhaustion and detachment. Hyacine had seen this man injured beyond repair, dragged from battle to battle back to the fullness of his health —yet only a handful of times had she seen the alpha this exhausted. This out of it.

Even so, Mydei held the white-haired Alpha in his arms, his protective grip as if he’s hiding him from the watchful gaze.

Phainon was curled against his chest, tucked beneath the prince’s chin, drawn in on himself like something small and wounded. It was also a sight Hyacine had never expected to witness.

And yes, her eyes did caught a glimpse of crimson at Phainon’s fingertips, claws still slick where they clutched desperately at Mydei.

She steadied herself, though her thoughts were already running too quickly, answering questions that she dared not to fill in the gaps herself. Not right now. Not without a proper explanation. The smell of blood still clung heavy in her sensitive nose.

“Lord Mydei,” Hyacine said softly, steadying her tone, though a faint tremor betrayed her unease. She could not begin to piece together what had happened here.

No answer came. The prince sat motionless, still cradling Phainon as though the world itself was barred from reaching them.

She tried again, stepping abit closer.

“Lord Mydei—”

A low growl rumbled answered instead.

Mydei couldn’t remember how he ended up on the floor, or when exactly the soldiers had hurried in. What he did remember was Phainon clinging onto him—the sting behind his eyes, the pounding headache that refused to fade, his skull throbbing in time with his racing heart. His thoughts were too clouded, too muddled, yet he had managed to stop, just a second too late—when the Alpha from the mated pair earlier tried to run away, despite Mydei clearly warning them not to.

He remembered the red crystals bursting, stopping more than one individual in their tracks. But truthfully, he hadn’t cared. Everything had been too much—the scents, the noises, all of it gnawing at his senses. The only thing he wanted was the man in his arms, hidden away from the chaos, sheltered from these grating sounds that clawed at his mind.

And somewhere along the line, he had slid down onto the floor. The Okheman soldiers had barged in. They had tried to confront him—or did they? Did he shoo them off? Did they hesitate when no reply came? He couldn’t quite recall.

Everything felt too much.

Almost… uncomfortable.

Yet, despite the haze, his focus never strayed from the man in his arms. Still, his mind wasn’t all with him—odd. Usually he had control. He prided himself on being capable, more than capable. Was it the earlier events wearing him down, or something else entirely? He couldn’t tell.

All he knew was he hadn’t even registered when Hyacine came in, calling for him.

Until

“Lord Mydei—”

A low growl rumbled against his chest.

Not from him.

The sound snapped him from his haze instantly. Mydei’s eyes widened in realization just as the man on his lap moved, almost snapping his head back. Mydei grabbed a fistful of white hair and forced him down before he could lash out, wincing when sharp teeth dug into his shoulder.

Bitten… This little savage.

The rumbling growl didn’t falter, nor did the slight struggle in his arms. But Mydei’s grip didn’t waver either. He held firm, the man pressed tightly against him.

With a tired sigh, he glanced at the shocked Omega standing in front of him.

“I’m sorry, Hyacine, but please stay a step back—“

His words cut off in a hiss as the bratty Alpha on his lap clawed his back, nails digging in hard enough to sting. Mydei smacked him lightly with his free hand, earning a growl himself.

HKS.

Hyacine nodded, stepping back, though hesitation still painted her face. Mydei swallowed down the urge to bite, to calm Phainon the way he should—to make the struggling Alpha behave. But poor Hyacine didn’t need to see all that.

Whatever helplessness showed in his expression must have been enough, because Hyacine suddenly darted off, then came rushing back with something clutched in her hand.

A syringe.

Oh.

Well, that would be helpful.

So Mydei tightened his hold on Phainon, hugging him with a force the man had likely never experienced in his entire life—tight enough to nearly knock the breath out of him. The Alpha writhed, but Mydei didn’t relent.

The healer omega, skilled as she was, didn’t waste a second. Swift and precise, she sank the needle into Phainon’s neck. Both she and Mydei braced at once when their fellow Heir gave a broken whimper, a small sound that slipped out before he sagged against Mydei, finally going limp.

A beat passed.

Only when Mydei was certain Phainon was out cold did he finally loosen his hold, releasing a breath he hadn’t realized he was holding. Still alert, still tense—but able to breathe.

Hyacine sank to the floor beside him with a soft exhale, just as exhausted as he was. Catching the doubt lingering in his eyes, she offered him a tired, reassuring smile.

“Oh, don’t worry, Lord Mydei. These are specially made knock out even the strongest Chrysos Heirs,” she said innocently, waving the syringe like it wasn’t anything alarming. “It should keep him asleep for the next few hours.”

Mydei glared at the syringe. As innocent and caring as Hyacine was, she had the same unnerving way of explaining things as Anaxagoras—like she hadn’t just admitted she carried sedatives strong enough for Heirs in her pocket. But who was he to complain? She had every right.

Adjusting the sleeping Alpha on his lap, Mydei shifted him carefully, making him presentable for the healer’s inspection. He gently laid Phainon onto the floor but kept the man’s head resting on his lap, his hand running absentmindedly through the ragged mess of white hair.

Hyacine moved quickly again, examining wounds and assessing any damage the unconscious Heir might have sustained. Her eyes lingered on a fresh bite mark just below the sun tattoo—so faint she might have missed it if the slightly torn shirt collar hadn’t revealed it.

She caught herself staring too long, only for Mydei’s scoff to cut through.

“That man,” he said before she could ask, “that lowlife tried to find an opening by biting down.” His tone was sharp, disgusted, as his gaze flicked away toward the obvious bloodstains on the marble floor. His hand, however, stayed possessively caressing the white hair between his fingers.

“It led to this.”

His words confirmed Hyacine’s earlier speculation, and then he continued, voice edged with a bitter laugh.

“That man might also be our prime suspect.” He laughed again, though it sounded hollow—mad, almost. Everything was oddly out of place, a chaos he couldn’t untangle, yet here he was, sitting cross-legged on the floor, explaining all of it like a madman. As much as he wanted that man gone from his sight, right now there were bigger issues. Damaging issues. And unfortunately, they involved keeping that bastard alive.

“Do try to keep him alive.”

From me he didn’t quite add.

Phainon woke up strangely groggy. He felt like he’d just come out of a long dream, but also like he’d been run over by ten sprinting Dromas. And unlike his usual terrors, the dream had been… comforting? Unnaturally so. He couldn’t quite recall any of it right now. Anyhow it didn’t change the fact that he felt like absolute shit. His entire body was heavy, achy in places he couldn’t pinpoint, but he needed to get up and look at the time.

Blinking blearily, he tried to chase off the sleepiness. He shouldn’t be slacking like this. He needed to get up.

Except—when he tried to sit, something yanked him straight back down.

It felt like he was being held down.

He squinted, still half-asleep.

Now that he was actually looking, not really but the room didn’t look like his. The structure was similar, sure, but the interior was completely different. Neater. Don’t get him wrong—he was usually neat too, he just…didn’t always have the time to clean up, that’s all.

And most importantly—what the hell was this thing keeping him from standing up?

He tried again, but the strong grip only made him fall onto his side, his head hitting the pillow with an off. Slowly, trying to shift around, his surroundings began registering—the warm air brushing over his nape, the way his back awkwardly pushed into something warm and solid. He froze when he heard a low, incoherent huff, the grip around him tightening. Then came the block of heat pressed fully into his back. And worse—something warm and wet dragged against the back of his neck, making him shiver.

And then, bit by bit, the haze cleared enough for the horrifying realization to set in. There was indeed something behind him.

No—someone behind him. On the bed.

His brain snapped awake at once. Panic tried to bloom. Looking down in disbelief, he found a muscular arm draped across his clothed torso, pinning him firmly. His eyes darted further and nearly bulged out of his head—his thighs. His bare thighs. He wouldn’t have even noticed if it weren’t for the chill of air licking at his skin.

He stared longer than he should, confirming in horror that he was, in fact, not wearing anything down there. Thankfully, the long grayish shirt he was in covered just enough to preserve some dignity.

Focus, Phainon.

Focus.

The arm around him looked…familiar. Too familiar. Red markings stretched across the muscled forearm, and he only knew one man alive with markings like that. The very arm he often drooled— admired.

The arm of the Kremnoen prince.

He inhaled sharply, sniffing the room.

Undeniably, it was the scent of the undying Alpha, Mydeimos. His rival, his sparring partner and his friend.

The very Alpha currently pressed against his back, nose buried against his neck, breathing evenly —peacefully unaware. Meanwhile, Phainon was doing everything in his power not to lose it completely.

Do not panic, Phainon.

This could just be a dream.

Just another one of those rut-dreams. Like all the others where a single encounter with the Alpha left him restless, rutting against his sheets unraveling like a—

He bit his lip hard enough to sting. The pain didn’t ground him. Didn’t calm the turmoil spiking higher by the second.

Because this was not a dream.

For half a heartbeat, his brain scrambled for some insane explanation. Maybe this was one of those scenarios out of Castorise’s borrowed novels—those ridiculous stories where people were whisked away to alternate realities designed to fulfill their deepest, filthiest desires.

He mentally smacked himself.

No. Idiot. He could clearly see the Dawn Device lit, hovering in plain sight beyond the cracked window. He was still in Amphoreus.

And somehow in Mydei’s bed.

Between Mydei’s arms.

Reeking of Mydei’s scent.

Face burning, a million thoughts running through his head—the smell of Mydei’s strong scent wasn’t helping at all. Head feeling heavy he asked himself:

What happened?

Why was he half-naked?

Why was he in Mydei’s bed?

Why wasn’t he screaming bloody murder?

His scent must have shifted, traitorous and betraying him—because the grip around him tightened again, Mydei’s body sliding impossibly closer until there was no space left. Phainon squirmed, trying to shift, but the arm was iron, unrelenting.

He dared to crane his neck, just enough to glimpse the Alpha. But the moment he moved, the hand at his stomach shifted—pressing firmly down over his lower stomach that—

“Nghh—!?”

The embarrassing sound ripped from him before he could stop it. He slapped a hand over his mouth, face flaming.

The hand stilled.

Phainon froze, mortified. In the small motion of turning, his bare ass brushed back against something—something warm. He didn’t want to think about it. Couldn’t. His face burned so hot it might as well combust.

Kaphale, why must it be this awkward. He just woke up!

And now, he meets the familiar pair of gold eyes. Awake. Staring right at him.

Another unfamiliar, pathetic noise left his throat before he could choke it back.

Phainon held his breath, still caught in the stare. Gold met blue, sharp and unblinking, and for a second he thought Mydei was wide awake, fully aware of what just happened. But then—no. Something was off. Those eyes weren’t sharp at all. They looked hazy, distant, a faint red bleeding into the gold.

“Mydei?” Phainon frowned, his gut twisting when he received no answer.

He shifted, trying to ease himself away—but the smallest motion was all it took. In a blink, he was flipped, manhandled onto his back, Mydei’s weight bearing down. A sharp slam of palm against the mattress caged him in, one hand on either side, leaving Phainon staring up at him, breath caught.

Gulping, Phainon’s eyes held the stare for a moment before reality came crashing in as his gaze drifted downward. As much as he’d like to keep up the staring contest, the fact was—he was still bare down there, and the damn shirt (probably Mydei’s), the thin layer of clothing he wore at the moment, wasn’t built for being thrown around. Which meant the cloth had revealed far more than he’d like.

Flushing from pure embarrassment, his hands flew on instinct to cover his dignity. But Mydei caught on instantly, grabbing his wrists and pinning them flat on either side of his head.

Phainon let out a small gasp, struggling, but his body felt heavier than usual. Uneasy. Unsteady. Too shaken to properly fight back against the man above him.

He gave a huff of disbelief, voice caught between anger and panic. “Mydei, you—”

The words got stuck in his throat.

Because Mydei’s face was lowered. Dangerously close—too close—for comfort. Phainon felt ragged breaths ghost against his skin, heat washing over his face. And Mydei’s eyes—titans, those were the same eyes he only saw when they sparred. When they lost themselves in the heat of battle. That gaze. Intense. Predatory.

Was Mydei trying to beat his ass here?

On the bed?

Right now?

What?

Phainon didn’t know. But the moment the Alpha leaned impossibly close, right up to his face, he turned his head sharply, eyes squeezing shut, bracing for the worst.

He’s going to die, isn’t he?

This was it.

Phainon, what had you done this time to make Mydei angry enough to kill you on the spot?

Oh, Kaphale, why must his life end here?

His life been short.

He still had so much to do.

Yet his miserable one-sided demise short lived as what he imagined never came.

Instead, Phainon snapped his eyes open at the sudden tickle on his neck.

The Alpha had nuzzled into his neck.

Blinking, confused, he stilled. Feeling the way Mydei’s nose pressed against his skin, and then the air shifted—flooded with the sharp, smoky scent of sandalwood, thick and cloying, like it wasn’t already suffocating the room.

Phainon tried to move, but the weight above him held him trapped. The scent was overwhelming, dizzying. And before he could stop himself, he had whimpered, almost arching against the bed trying to move. In a futile attempt to put distance between himself as the tickling press of Mydei’s nose and breath, he accidentally bared his neck. Unknowingly.

And then came a low satisfied rumble.

Instead of filling him with awkwardness or discomfort, the sound left him—strangely content. Inexplicably.

Huh…?

He should be mad furious for being handled like this.

His Alpha’s pride should’ve been ushered to shreds!

But then why was he happy that Mydei sounded satisfied?

The nose trailed its way up, brushing along his jaw, to his face. Lips ghosted against his skin—soft, grazing touches that sent shivers racing down his spine. Every nerve lit up. The Alpha’s grip on his arms was like iron, unyielding, immovable.

Shamelessly, Mydei rubbed against his cheek, nuzzling impossibly closer.

And he heard another low rumble.

Phainon was so distracted by everything—the weight, the scent, the warmth—that he didn’t even register it at first.

Was Mydei… purring?

But to his horror, it wasn’t Mydei who was purring.

The sound was coming from his own chest.

Phainon blinked, stunned, unable to begin processing what was even happening. Mydei’s face was still buried against his own, like some satisfied cat, and worse—he himself was enjoying it. He didn’t know how it had gotten to this point, how much he’d missed, how much he couldn’t piece together. His reactions were all wrong, all odd.

But he had to push the questions aside. Right now, there was only one priority: he needed Mydei to wake up.

So, as bravely as his shaky, dry voice could manage, he whispered:

“Mydei…?”

He prayed the words would reach him.

But luck ran thin.

Nothing.

No response. Only the drag of Mydei’s nose sliding along his jaw.

“H-hey—snap out of it.” Phainon nudged him gently with his face, desperate to jolt him back.

This time, he did get a reply.

A low growl.

Phainon swallowed hard, praying the man wouldn’t accidentally tear his throat out. He tried again, firmer, voice breaking,

“Mydei—hey, wake up, you—”

He cut off with a sharp gasp.

Because Mydei had licked him.

The Alpha’s tongue pressed against his neck, leaving behind wet heat.

Phainon’s thoughts scattered. His body heated, reacting unconsciously to every touch.

This—this wasn’t working.

He shifted again, but this time testing the weight holding him down. His arms were useless, pinned, but his legs—his legs were free. Barely.

Good.

Ignoring the way his clothes shifted, baring more than he’d ever want, he wrapped his legs around Mydei’s waist. He could worry about decency later. For now—he needed leverage.

He flexed, muscles straining, grip tightening around the Alpha’s waist. Gathering every scrap of strength left in his body, he shoved. Hard.

And just like that, the tables turned.

Phainon forced Mydei onto his back, pinning him down, arms finally freed. The Alpha huffed beneath him, dissatisfied, hands twitching like claws ready to seize prey again.

But before he could, Phainon went for the only solution that came to mind in that instant.

He gripped Mydei’s shoulders hard, threw his head back, and slammed their foreheads together.

Praying—desperately—that it would wake the Alpha up.

The impact was harder than it should’ve been. He even heard a soft crack, hoping it was nothing brutal as it sounded as stars exploded across his vision.

A few beats passed as he rested his forehead on Mydei’s, trying to clear the dark spots. Then slowly he lifted his head.

Clearing the dots from his vision, which was still blurred a bit, he could make out Mydei’s face. The latter also had his eyes shut. And then they slowly opened.

Phainon scanned the face underneath him while breathing heavily.

The gold eyes looked awake again. Clear. The red that had bled through was gone, replaced with the bright, sharp gold he was used to seeing.

They both panted, lungs dragging like the room had no air left to give.

Smiling a bit, he huffed a breathy laugh. “Well good morning to you too, Mydei—”

But then he felt it. Something hot trailing down his forehead. His vision flickering.

He blinked, trying to focus.

He then saw the way those cleared golden eyes from the Alpha under him widened, mouth opening —in shock? In attempt to say something? He didn’t know, he couldn’t hear it though. Then he saw a small drop of gold landing on Mydei’s face. Possibly his. He didn’t know—he could barely see it after all.

He might’ve hit his head a little too hard, he guessed. Because yes, the world was kind of spinning as he heard a faint calling of his name. But it was muffled.

Damn this Kremnoen forehead of his. What was it made of, iron?

Phainon had barely registered the horrified look Mydei had right now. If he could, he would’ve commented on it, given the snarky remark like ‘wasn’t fear not mentioned in the Kremnoen dictionary?’—but the words were stuck in his throat.

He smiled faintly instead, giving one last look at those golden eyes.

And then the world blurred into spots, his body collapsing forward before darkness finally embraced him.

When Phainon woke again, he felt lighter than before. Not weighed down, not heavy—honestly, he felt almost too light, like his body wasn’t his own.

Slowly, carefully, he blinked open his eyes. The first thing he registered was that he was still in Mydei’s bed. Still in Mydei’s room. But this time, he was alone, tangled up in the sheets. His head turned, scanning the space, just to be sure. No one. Still, instead of getting up right away, he sank further into the mattress, letting himself breathe and clear his thoughts. He wasn’t in a rush. His body needed the pause.

He inhaled taking a deep breathe—and the distant smell of toast and eggs drifted in. His stomach growled instantly, loud and demanding. That familiar tug of hunger hit him like a reminder that, he needed to eat.

With a tiny shred of courage, he glanced down. Sheets twisted between his legs, messy and wrinkled. But this time—thank Kaphale—he was wearing pants. Pants. Actual pants. He blinked, relief rushing through him in a wave that made his face heat. Mydei must have helped him into them. Silently, Phainon was grateful, though the thought also made him flush even deeper. Mydei had definitely seen him bare, then. He shoved that mortifying thought aside before it could spiral.

Stretching, his muscles strained and popped from sleep, and he jolted upright with a sharp motion —only to immediately groan. His head throbbed, stabbing pain blooming at his temple.

Oh. Right. He hit his head.

His hand lifted to his forehead, wincing when his fingers pressed against a sting. But instead of raw skin, his touch met a patch—a neat white plaster covering the injury.

The sound he made must have been loud, because the next thing he knew, the door slammed open. Mydei barged in, wearing nothing but an apron and a pair of pants, holding a plate piled with food.

Phainon had stared for bit then his face lit up instantly, ridiculously bright. Because Mydei? Domestic? Mydei with food? This was straight out of one of his fever dreams. He actually beamed, a grin tugging wide at his lips as his hands instinctively reached out, grabby and childlike. Still buried in the sheets, he wordlessly asked for it.

The other Alpha huffed, disbelief written all over his face, but he shook his head anyway. He stepped closer, setting the plate on the bed beside Phainon, sitting down at the edge.

But before Phainon could even reach for the food, Mydei had already picked up the fork, scooping a piece, and brought it straight to his mouth. Waiting. Expecting him to open.

Phainon blinked.

The gesture—it was so normal. Something so natural and kind. Something so delicate, thoughtful. If it weren’t coming from the Undying Prince, Mydeimos. The same Alpha responsible for countless of Phainon’s battered visits to the twilight courtyard after their ‘friendly’ sparring matches. The same hands holding the fork with such gentleness were the very hands that had thrown him across training grounds like a ragdoll. And yet here he was, feeding him like a mate.

Phainon’s jaw dropped before he could stop it. And Mydei took it as a cue, promptly shoving the fork into his mouth.

Phainon muffled a sound of protest, but chewed anyway, the taste of eggs spreading across his tongue. Then Mydei calmly went for another piece.

Wait. Wait. Was he hallucinating? Or had he actually get teleported into those alternate realities— straight out of Castorise’s novels? Or had he hit his head so hard when they bonked foreheads that now he was losing his mind? Because this—this was bizarre. One of the strangest mornings of his life. The constant whiplash since he’d opened his eyes was making it hard to keep up.

He chewed slowly, swallowing, then turned to glance at Mydei again. The Alpha looked… tired. More tired than Phainon had seen him in a long while.

When Mydei lifted the fork again, Phainon gently shook his head, a small smile tugging at his lips. “Well, thank you, but I can feed myself, if you don’t mind.”

He meant no offense, none at all. But Mydei’s brows furrowed, his head tilting like he was trying to decode the words. Cute. For a second, Phainon wondered if he’d accidentally spoken in a foreign language. Not that he knew many.

He reached for the plate to take it, maybe thank Mydei for his hospitality, when a strong hand suddenly shot up to his face. Mydei’s palm cupped his chin, tilting his head up, holding him steady. And then the distance between them closed, just enough that Mydei could stare straight into his face.

Phainon’s breath stilled. The man’s gaze roamed his features, inspecting, shifting his head with the lightest pressure of his hand, back and forth, observing every detail. Golden eyes locked onto him, sharp and focused, and Phainon flushed hard under the weight of it. They were close. Far too close. And yet, Phainon let him.

Finally, Mydei’s examination ended. His voice broke the silence, even, calm, but with an edge Phainon knew all too well. “You’re awake.”

It was said simply. But Phainon could hear the irritation hidden beneath.

He forced a shrug, offering a sheepish smile. “Awake than ever.” Then, almost embarrassed, he ducked his face away, slipping from Mydei’s grip. “Sorry for… you know, slamming our heads together earlier.”

Mydei’s mouth opened, then closed. Then he huffed. “That’s not what I meant.”

Phainon blinked, confusion knitting his brows. “Huh?”

The Prince sighed, like he had already expected this, his golden eyes flickering down—just for a breath, just for a blink towards Phainon’s neck.

“So you don’t remember anything, I assume.”

Phainon tilted his head. Memory fuzzy, thoughts hazy. He knew something had happened, but the details slipped through him like water. The light throb in his forehead wasn’t helping either.

Mydei waited. But silence was answered enough. His sigh deepened, tired, resigned. At last, he pushed the plate into Phainon’s hands.

“You missed a lot. Eat first. We’ll discuss everything later.” His words trailed off, then his nose wrinkled faintly, his face shaded with the barest hint of pink. “And you need a shower.”

And so their breakfast-in-bed conversation was cut short. It wasn’t even breakfast, Mydei corrected him—it was almost past action hour. At that, Phainon nearly choked on his food, halfway ready to bolt from the quarters. Mydei, irritated, soothed him with a remark that Aglaea had granted them some time. Phainon didn’t buy it, but sat down anyway.

It was almost going normally, calmly even, with Mydei giving him fresh towels and asking if he needed anything—to Phainon’s surprise, how genuinely worried this man was for him for some reason.

“What am I, a child?” Phainon waved him off with a crooked grin, stepping into Mydei’s bathroom.
